The Long TableEssay

THEslow history of the kitchen table

Four rooms, three tables and the people who kept them, told in the order the chairs were added.

Placeholder essay text. Every house in the street had a table before it had a sofa, and most of the arguments that mattered happened across one. This specimen shows the text cut at reading size with old-style figures, as in 1924 or 1968.

The display cut stays above 40 px. Below that its hairlines thin out, so the deck and the body use the text cut, which was drawn for small sizes.

BY THE EDITORS · ESSAY

Settings

Display
Libre Caslon Display OFL
Text
Libre Caslon Text OFL · body, deck and the italic swap word
Moves
serif display, mixed-case editorial
Mood
literary, considered, warm, unhurried
Case
Sentence case for headlines; one word per headline swapped into the italic at the same size; labels in tracked capitals at 13 px.
Numerals and features
font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums proportional-nums; font-feature-settings: "liga" 1, "dlig" 1

Issue 1924 · pages 36 to 48Issue 1924 · pages 36 to 48

Old-style figures sit inside reading text; switch to lining only in tables.
Signature
The italic swap: one word of a roman display line set in the text italic at display size, so the line changes voice mid-sentence.
Use when
Long reads, essays, publishers, cultural newsletters, any page whose job is to be read slowly.
Turns into slop when
When every headline gets an italic word (it becomes a tic), when the italic word is also coloured (the coloured keyword tell), or when it heads a SaaS page that has nothing to say.
Offline
Without network the page falls back to the system stacks in --f-display and --f-text; no font files ship with this specimen.
